# Chaotic Good Computing

> Articles for the data and engineering consulting practice Chaotic Good Computing, as well as personal notes by Spencer Elkington.

Each page below links to a Markdown copy of it: the page's address with `.md` after it. A copy opens with the page's address, author, dates and tags.

## Articles

- [GPTinglish: Unnatural Language Processing](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/binglish.md): The only market crashing is the market for sanitized language. Stay human. Embrace typos.
- [Don't Double Down: Structured Streaming to Wrangle Data](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/structured-streaming.md): Stop reprocessing your entire dataset every time new data arrives. A practical guide to Spark Structured Streaming with code examples and cost logic.
- [Littlefield Simulator: The Art of Laziness](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/littlefield.md): Efficiency: spending six hours building a web scraper to avoid five minutes of daily work. Automating a business simulation because checking in is for chumps.
- [The Unbearable Weight of ROBLOX Celebrity](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/robloxaville.md): Being famous online in 2009 is the highest high I'll ever reach. A love letter to the coolest dork I know, hatemail for client-side exploits, and a limitless supply of Monopoly dollars.
- [Say Goodbye to Untitled (5) — GitHub Actions for Resumes](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/resume-ci-pipeline.md): Set up continuous integration to auto-update your resume everywhere. Overleaf, GitHub, and LaTeX automation for the perpetually disorganized.
- [Hello, Blog! (Posts by a dummy, for other dummies)](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/articles/hello-blog.md): The obligatory "Hello!" post to suss out what this site will be. Python examples as unnecessary as the post itself.

## Annotations

- [Planning With Agents: Better can be Better](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/highlights/maggieappleton.com/Planning-with-Agents-Divided-Worlds,-Boundary-Objects,-and-Thicker-Interfaces.md): Annotations on Maggie Appleton's 2026 talk about Boundary Objects
- [Tell the speakers that you liked their talks](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/highlights/ohhelloana.blog/Tell-the-speakers-that-you-liked-their-talks.md): Some quick thoughts on Ana Rodrigues's post "Tell the speakers that you liked their talks", and a general initial test for web-based annotations.
- [Union types (C# reference)](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/highlights/learn.microsoft.com/Union-types-C-reference.md): Some quick notes on the Union type addition in C# 15, and how I can use it to make Flowthru fail-fast(er)
- [Writing Better Gherkin](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/highlights/cucumber.io/Writing-better-Gherkin-Cucumber.md): A few notes on a very important, but hidden, part of the Cucumber and Gherkin documentation around Behavior Driven Development
- [Lean Software Development: Prelude Notes](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/lean-software-development/00-prelude.md): Notes on the prelude chapters of Lean Software Development (2003)
- [Working with Valves: Understanding the Structure of "Flat" Organizations](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/valve-handbook.md): Many an engineer has heard tales of Valve's "flat" organization structure — what is fact, what is fiction, and how does it actually work? An annotated copy of the 2012 First Edition of Valve's Employee Handbook.
- [It's All Graphs, Dummy](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/theory-of-stupidity.md): Our lives are all dominated by a little graph in our hearts — and sometimes, that graph gets wacky. A review of Dietrich Bonhoeffer's "Theory of Stupidity", part of his larger ~1943-1945 work "Letters and Papers from Prison."
- [Hyperparameter verification of StcE protein folds in Pedram et al., 2023](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/bertozzi-stickies.md): The rubber hits the road on ColabFold! I hope that's rubber I'm smelling — although it may be the computer. A replication attempt of a protein fold figure in K. Pedram et al (2023).
- [An Annotated Guide to Hobbyist Protein Folding](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/protein-folding-for-fun.md): Amaze (or bore) your friends and family by picking up on a hot new hobby that's all the rage — protein folding! An annotated starter to the 2021 paper "ColabFold - Making protein folding accessible to all"
- [Agentic Programming as Theory Building](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/programming-as-theory-building.md): Do humans have a role in software development anymore? Absolutely — but we need to rethink what it means to program. An modern review of Peter Naur's 1985 essay "Programming as Theory Building"
- [APL: Pattern 4; Agricultural Valleys](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/04-agricultural-valleys.md): Urban development has the high ground over agricultural and ecological preservation — and it should! *A Pattern Language* annotations on Pattern 4: Agricultural Valleys
- [APL: Pattern 5; Lace of Country Streets](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/05-lace-of-country-streets.md): How dense is too dense? How sparse is too sparse? Annotations for A Pattern Language's proposals for the density of metro-adjacent country streets for agriculture, recreation, and preservation.
- [APL: Pattern 1; Independent Regions](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/01-independent-regions.md): Home isn't where the heart is — it's a single node on a very, very large graph. Annotations for the "Independent Regions" pattern of *A Pattern Language*.
- [APL: Pattern 2; The Distribution of Towns](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/02-the-distribution-of-towns.md): How close is too close? How far is too far? *A Pattern Language* annotations related to the statistical, economic, and ecologic concerns in balancing how dense human habitats ought to be.
- [APL: Pattern 3; City Country Fingers](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/03-city-country-fingers.md): City, with natural stripes — or nature, with city stripes? Annotations for A Pattern Language, and tracking public opinion of where Americans want to live over the past 50 years.
- [APL: Pattern 0; Introduction](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/a-pattern-language/00-introduction.md): Can graphs be libertarian? Authoritarian? Annotations for the introductory portion of the 1977 book A Pattern Language.
- [Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/evolutions-revolutions.md): Annotations for Greiner's 1972 paper "Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow", about the structural composition of organizations at different sizes and requirements.
- [LLMs: A Primer Presentation for Our Newest, Scariest Tool](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/llm-starter.md): An engineer-focused primer on the mechanisms that drive Large Language Models. Basics on how we got here, how they work, and how to use them without feeling an apocalyptic dread.
- [The Simple Economics of Open Source](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/simple-economics-of-open-source.md): Why do we do what we do? "Egoboo." Exploring economic models of OSS contributions beyond altruism and ego.
- [Annotations: College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/annotations/college-admissions-and-the-stability-of-marriage.md): A dive into the hottest algorithm of the 1960s: Gale-Shapley matchmaking. Who knew that the mysteries of the heart could be solved with a matrix?

## Notes

- [The Wild Web](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/the-wild-web.md): Come with me and explore an invisible social network: IndieWeb, where the cowboy can-do attitude of Web 1.0 is alive and a-thrivin'.
- [You can pry my dashes from my cold, dead hands](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/dashes.md): A bit of self-reflection on dashes in my writing to decide if LLMs have rotted my brain, or if my brain was already beyond saving from the start.
- [Chipotleware](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/agronomic-software-side-note.md): A brief side-rant about the (former) burrito-style economics of junior-level software engineering
- [Software Gardening](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/software-gardening.md): Garden-inspired development as a non-sinister, people-centric way to think about post-LLM software development
- [Security Alert: Softlock and ACE via Natural Language Overload](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/natural-language-cve.md): I think I’ve found a pretty large CVE that has gone without a formal report, despite absolutely saturating the field of software engineering. It’s subtle and…
- [Ants in the Neighborhood](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/ants-in-the-neighborhood.md): Is Jane Street run by soccer-loving ants? Inconclusive. We *can* conclude that they're fans of Markov Chains, though — an invaluable tool for understanding complex data structures.
- [A Pattern Language, and a Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/pattern-languages-of-the-neighborhood.md): The beginning of a topological review of the 1977 urban design and architecture reference book A Pattern Language, and a journey to understand Earth's greatest graph: the Earth, itself.
- [Quick Fix: Tone Down Obsidian List/Header Padding](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/fixing-obsidian-paddings-and-margins.md): Annoyed by Obsidian Live Preview over-padding headers and aggressively indenting? Some snippets to help keep your notes from jumping around, so you can focus on actually writing them.
- [Dice Roll Distribution Widget](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/scratch/dice-widget.md): Discover the probability distributions of different dice roll combinations
- [The Advantages of Advantage: Intro to Probability Convolutions](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/roll-advantage.md): What *is* the advantage of rolling with advantage? Exploring dice roll combinations and probability convolutions.
- [Quartz Widgets: Graphs, Galore!](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/mdx-widgets-test.md): I killed 4 of my blogs trying to implement MDX support. Will this one be next? Using MDX with Quartz to create interactive graphs, diagrams, and demos — clear as day.
- [How to Run Your Own Hostage Negotiation](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/hostage-negotiations.md): LLMs: Are we doomed to die, or born to garden? I'd like to make the case that AI is less like Terminator, and more like tomatoes.
- [Intro to Event Storming](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/event-storming-intro.md): Notes from learning Event Storming for domain-driven design. Thoughts on phases, color-coded chaos, and how to transition from fast pitches to full products.
- [Kickoff: Season of Systems](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/kickoff-season-of-systems.md): I'm learning to live with the systems that stole my beloved em-dash. A season dedicated to negotiating how to live with the agentic models that have turned my career upside-down.
- [Review: Season of Rhythm](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/season-of-rhythm-in-review.md): Looking back at my year-long attempt to build up long-lasting habits. A retrospective on routines, remote work transitions, and learning the art of slow-and-steady.
- [Terraform LocalStack Testing](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/scratch/terraform-localstack.md): $70/mo/seat? Just using live AWS may be cheaper. An evaluation of LocalStack as a testbed for Account Factory Terraform.
- [Feeling Right, Nothing Done: Don't Be the Death of Consensus](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/strong-and-weak-opinions.md): Classifying opinions as "strong" or "weak" to stop wasting hours in fruitless engineering debates. How consensus can beat being "right", and an open letter for the tactically apathetic.
- [Before You Slabtop Your Laptop: A Brief Warning](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/scratch/warning-about-slabtops.md): PSA: Check if your laptop needs an LCD for POST before removing the screen. Learned this the hard way after 5 hours and a fried motherboard. Learn from my dumb mistakes.
- [Turning SelfControl into Self Restraint](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/putting-selfcontrol-on-raycast.md): Building a Raycast plugin to schedule website blocks — because checking news "just one more time" destroys flow. Automate SelfControl and self control: take your laptop back.
- [Caveat Lector: Reader Beware](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/caveat-lector.md): I'm embracing being wrong on the internet in an effort to learn in public. A disclaimer on digital gardening, dead pixels, and the fear of terminal online-ness.
- [Some initial thoughts about time tracking](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/time-tracking.md): Initial thoughts on using tools like Apple Shortcuts and Timery/Toggle for tracking how I spend my time -- every minute of every day.
- [The Quest to Slay The Goblin](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/the-quest-to-slay-the-goblin.md): My life devolves into sleep-eat-procrastinate cycles without structure—I call this "The Goblin." Productivity tools, hating on hustle culture, and a new definition for horticulture.
- [Quantitative Analysis of Markets & Organizations](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/qamo.md): My time at the University of Utah was longer than I'd planned, cut shorter than expected by COVID-19. I was very lucky to have mentorship to push me across the finish line.
- [Breaking Ground on Digital Gardening](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/digital-gardening-with-quartz.md): Why I stopped hoarding 60%-done drafts and started publishing messy thoughts instead. Embracing digital gardening, from-chaos-to-cultivated, and a healthy dose of imperfection.
- [In Review: The (bad) 2017 Robloxaville Remaster](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/robloxaville-remaster.md): How over-engineering killed a 3-month remaster of an old ROBLOX game. Looking back at the depth of Dunning-Kruger, and how good code doesn't make a good game.
- [Kickoff: Season of Rhythm](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/kickoff-season-of-rhythm.md): "Fight or flight" is a rough way to treat white-collar life. My Season of Rhythm is dedicated to transitioning from constant sprints to slow-and-steady.
- [The Over/Unders of Over- and Under-Engineering](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/over-under-engineering.md): I've learned so much in my career — so why do I finish fewer projects than I used to? Over-engineering: it's easier to be bad at something on accident than on purpose.
- [How to Write a Resume in Typst](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/typst-resume-template.md): A beginner-friendly and guided resume starter for Typst users! Great for anybody looking to easily maintain and adapt their resume to new applications.
- [Entries to SOME 1](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/scratch/some1-entry.md): Stable matching, optimal stopping, and Bachelor analysis - visualized with some care.
- [Utah Office Consult](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/utah-office-consult.md): People problems are the hardest engineering problems. A consult on thinking out-of-the-box to explain morale problems in small companies.
- [College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/stability-of-marriage.md): My college presentation on the Gale-Shapley paper, recorded on an iPad, like a true professional. Non-market environments, matchmaking lattices, and gratitude for good professors.
- [Reading the Room with Beethoven](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/beethoven.md): A HackTheU 2019 project for real-time live captioning using remote microphones.
- [What *are* Supply Chains, Anyway?](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/supply-chain.md): A first foray into network visualization: messy graphs, abject terror. Early data viz experiments searching for supply loops. Bad graphs; interesting questions.
- [Quicksort: Every CS Student's Favorite Algorithm, Scratched Up](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/literal-scratch-quicksort.md): Implementing QuickSort in Scratch. Its only real-world accomplishment? Wearing out my mouse's scroll bar.
- [Scratch Piano Application](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/notes/literal-scratch-piano.md): An educational waveform visualizer written in everybody's favorite programming language: Scratch.

## Other writing

- [Math is Dead, and Pickles are Small](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/dead-math.md): To understand why OpenAI completely upended the world of mathematics with its proof that Navier-Stokes is not smooth in three dimensions, you must first understand that cucumbers of any size can be properly pickled.
- [The Season of Stamps](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/content/season-of-stamps.md): The kickoff post for my Season of Stamps: exploring new places, meeting new people, and putting the final stamp of approval on a back catalog of projects worth publishing.

## About the site

- [Work Resume](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/resume.md): The PDF copy of my day-to-day resume.
- [Privacy Policy](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/privacy.md): When it comes to collecting data, there's a fine line between making a good site and making an invasive product. To make this site more useful, I want to collect enough data to improve, but never enough to undermine anybody's privacy.
- [About Me](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/contact.md): The ultimate CAPTCHA: proof that I am a human, and how to get in contact with me!
- [AI Policy](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/ai-policy.md): I may not have any control about how AI affects me, but I can at least make a policy for how I use it.
- [Chaotic Good Computing](https://blog.chaoticgood.computer/index.md): Articles for the data and engineering consulting practice Chaotic Good Computing, as well as personal notes by Spencer Elkington.
